about.name: HIPAA-Compliant Local LLM for Medical Practices

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to use AI with patient data under HIPAA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — with the right architecture. Consumer cloud AI with PHI is a violation. On-premises AI where data never leaves your control is compliant by design. The difference is the architecture, not the tool.

mainEntity.name: What is a local LLM device?

acceptedAnswer.text: A self-contained AI appliance that runs on hardware your practice owns, on your premises. Models run locally, so patient data never leaves the building — no third-party processing, no training-data absorption.

mainEntity.name: Does a BAA make cloud AI HIPAA compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BAA makes a vendor contractually responsible for PHI they handle, and it's required for cloud AI that touches PHI. But it doesn't prevent the data from leaving your building — it just governs what happens after. On-premises AI removes the question entirely.

mainEntity.name: What hardware does a local LLM for a medical practice need?

acceptedAnswer.text: A modern workstation or small server with a GPU — typically one machine for most practices, racked on-premises and configured for encrypted, access-controlled use. Sizing depends on staff volume and workloads.

mainEntity.name: How much does a HIPAA-compliant local LLM setup cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hardware, deployment, and configuration are a fraction of what enterprise cloud AI contracts cost over time — and you own the hardware outright. Quotes are practice-specific because every build is sized differently.

mainEntity.name: Can a local LLM handle medical documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — for drafting, summarizing, and documentation workflows, local open-weight models (including medical-tuned models) perform at the level staff are already used to. They are not licensed medical devices and should never make clinical decisions — same as any LLM.

mainEntity.name: What does OCR actually penalize in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Missing risk analysis. OCR's 2026 enforcement pattern consistently punishes the absent risk assessment underneath a breach — not the breach itself. Documented risk analysis and controls are the difference between a defensible posture and a settlement.
